2026-09-23T12:35:31.5977150Z **Creating a Pull Request**
2026-09-23T12:35:31.5977740Z 
2026-09-23T12:35:31.5978143Z To create a pull request:
2026-09-23T12:35:31.5979308Z 1. Make any file changes directly in the working directory.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.5981598Z 2. If you haven't done so already, create a new local branch using `git checkout -b <branch-name>` with an appropriate unique name.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.5985258Z 3. Add and commit your changes to the branch. Be careful to add exactly the files you intend, and check there are no extra files left un-added. Verify you haven't deleted or changed any files you didn't intend to.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6002984Z 4. Do not push your changes. That will be done by the tool.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6005910Z 5. Create the pull request with the create_pull_request tool from safeoutputs exactly once, only when the final title/body/branch are ready.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6009195Z 6. After calling `create_pull_request`, STOP. Do not probe with another PR call, do not test auth with manual `git push`, and do not rewrite git remotes.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6010971Z 
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6015456Z **Important**: The `branch` parameter in the create_pull_request tool **must exactly match the name of your current local git branch** — the branch you just committed to. You can verify this with `git branch --show-current`. Never invent or guess a branch name; always use the actual branch name from `git branch --show-current`. If you are on an existing branch (e.g. you checked out a PR branch), use that branch name.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6020049Z 
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6023180Z **Important**: `create_pull_request` is not a sandbox. Every successful call records a real PR intent that can become an externally visible pull request. Never use placeholder payloads like `"test"` / `"test"` to see what happens. If you are not ready to open the real PR, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6027205Z </safe-output-tools>
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6028118Z <mcp-clis>
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6031338Z The following servers are available as CLI executables on `PATH`. Invoke them from bash when you need CLI transport. Unless a server is explicitly listed in another prompt section as an MCP tool (for example `<safe-output-tools>`), do not call these via an MCP tool interface.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6034416Z 
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6035012Z - `github` — run `github --help` to see available tools
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6036660Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6037590Z 
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6038118Z For `mcpscripts`, always use the CLI commands above.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6040690Z For `safeoutputs`, call the tool names listed in `<safe-output-tools>` directly; the `safeoutputs` CLI commands above are an optional equivalent transport.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6042564Z 
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6044718Z For `safeoutputs`, every successful call is a real write-intent declaration - do not use it for probing, auth checks, or placeholder payloads. Use `noop` or `report_incomplete` if not ready to emit the final action.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6047373Z 
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6048237Z For multiple or complex arguments, pipe a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel:
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6049781Z ```bash
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6050946Z printf '{"item_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody."}' | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6052704Z # or write to a file: safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6054060Z ```
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6054488Z 
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6060079Z **Multi-line or long `body` content:** do NOT build the JSON payload with `printf`/`echo` embedding raw newlines or many escaped characters directly in the command line — the sandbox's shell command-injection guard may reject long or complex quoted arguments (reporting "expansion patterns"/"command substitution" even though none are present) and retrying the identical command will fail again. Instead, write the content to a temp file with a heredoc, then use `jq -Rs` to inject it as the `body` field:
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6066001Z ```bash
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6066862Z cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/gh-aw/body.md
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6067850Z Title
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6068283Z 
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6068699Z Multi-line body content goes here.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6069711Z EOF
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6071069Z jq -Rs '{title: "My title", body: .}' /tmp/gh-aw/body.md | safeoutputs create_discussion .
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6072529Z ```
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6074525Z If a shell command is rejected for containing expansion patterns, do not retry the same command — switch to the heredoc + `jq -Rs` pattern above.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6076458Z 
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6077608Z To inject an entire local file as the `body` field without re-embedding its content in the model context, use `jq -Rs`:
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6079416Z ```bash
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6080370Z jq -Rs --arg discussion_number "$DISCUSSION_NUMBER" \
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6083019Z   '{discussion_number: ($discussion_number|tonumber), body: .}' \
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6084347Z   discussion-body.md \
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6085313Z   | safeoutputs update_discussion .
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6086533Z ```
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6089075Z `jq -Rs` reads the file as a raw string (`-R`) and slurps it into a single JSON string value (`-s`), so `body` is always a valid JSON field. Piping `cat file | safeoutputs ...` does not populate `body` and will be rejected.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6091447Z 
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6093079Z The generated command syntax above is schema-derived from each enabled tool's final `inputSchema` and is the source of truth for required/optional parameters.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6096381Z Use `<server> --help` and `<server> <tool> --help` for the same schema-derived signatures and examples before calling any command.
2026-09-23T12:35:31.6098279Z </mcp-clis>
